name: Carrion Defense Works Chemical Hazard Oversuit CHO-4
product_name: Carrion Defense Works Chemical Hazard Oversuit CHO-4
description: A full-body protective suit providing Level A chemical, biological, and radiological protection through a multi-layer barrier system with integrated self-contained breathing apparatus. The CHO-4 uses a laminate of chemical-resistant polymer, activated carbon fabric, and vapor-barrier membrane to create an impenetrable barrier against liquid, vapor, and particulate hazards. The suit includes 4 hours of breathing air, communication systems, and a heads-up display showing environmental threat data from integrated sensors. Carrion designed it for their own CBRN operations teams but sells it through their defense catalog.

specifications.protection level: EPA Level A — full CBRN encapsulation
specifications.layers: Chemical polymer + activated carbon + vapor barrier

story_hooks: A team wearing CHO-4 suits entered a contaminated zone and their suits' sensors detected a compound not in any hazard database — the unknown agent was penetrating the activated carbon layer, a protection failure that should be impossible.

CHO-4 suits have been stolen and modified for use in robberies — the full-body coverage and breathing apparatus make the wearer immune to tear gas and chemical deterrents while providing complete visual anonymity.

physical_description.visual_profile: A full-body encapsulation suit with a distinctive bulbous helmet featuring a wide transparent visor and integrated breathing apparatus. The suit presents as a continuous sealed garment from neck to ankles, with reinforced glove seals and boot covers. Heavy-duty construction with visible layering at joints and seams.
physical_description.dimensions: 180–200 cm tall when worn; approximately 60 cm shoulder width
physical_description.weight_description: 12 kg total with air supply — requires both hands to don/doff; worn as a complete system, not pocketable
physical_description.primary_material: Laminated chemical-resistant polymer composite exterior; inner activated carbon fabric layer; outer vapor-barrier membrane; silicone and neoprene seals at joints
physical_description.finish: Matte rippled surface with slight iridescence from the polymer laminate; textured grip zones at shoulders and thighs; non-reflective to minimize visual signature
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat industrial gray primary with high-visibility neon yellow striping along spine, wrists, and ankles; black silicone seals and trim
physical_description.interface_elements: Helmet visor with integrated heads-up display (cyan/green data overlay visible), communication microphone array integrated into mask, two rotary dials for air management on chest pack, quick-disconnect connectors for air supply (bright red), pressure gauge on shoulder harness, environmental sensor cluster (small circular array) mounted on sternum
distinctive_features: Oversized domed helmet with internal breathing apparatus visible through translucent sections
Integrated air tank/SCBA backpack mounted as spinal column element with pressure indicators
Yellow-and-gray chevron warning pattern on thighs and calves
Sealed finger compartments with individual articulation grooves
Bright chemical-hazard trefoil symbol on both shoulders
Red emergency deflation tabs at neck and ankles
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS logo (angular phoenix silhouette) stamped on left chest; EPA Level A certification hologram on right shoulder; batch/serial number on arm cuff; CBRN warning labels across lower back in three languages
physical_description.condition_typical: When deployed, suit shows use-worn polymer with minor scuff marks; air supply gauge visibly decreasing; HUD display active with threat-level readouts; gloves show talc residue from donning; equipment secured tightly at all closure points
